S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
examples: Makes mistakes in homework or tests by misreading questions or skipping important parts.
Frequently omits details or makes typos in work documents or reports.
Repeats mistakes in calculations or numerical work, such as switching signs or getting digits wrong.
Performs tasks incorrectly by missing important details in instructions.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
examples: Appears not to be listening, looking elsewhere or spacing out during conversation.
Immediately asks to repeat what was just said or instructed.
Does not respond when name is called or answers only after a long delay.
Misses the content of the conversation, giving unrelated answers or out-of-context reactions.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
examples: Constantly shaking legs or twisting and squirming body while seated.
Spinning a pen or fiddling with nearby objects, unable to keep hands still.
Continually changing posture and feeling uncomfortable while sitting.
Constantly moving, such as tapping the desk with fingers or tapping feet on the floor.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
examples: Frequently leaves seat or wanders around during class or meetings using excuses.
Unable to sit still during meals and keeps getting up.
Leaves seat in the middle of a movie or performance to go to the restroom or go outside.
Continually leaves seat and wanders around in the office where one is expected to sit and work.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
examples: Butts into conversations of others where they have not been invited.
Joins in on others' work or games without permission or interferes.
Touches or uses other people's belongings or work without permission.
Keeps talking to and disturbing others when they are focusing on work or studying.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation is a neurodevelopmental disorder marked by persistent hyperactivity and impulsivity that are excessive for developmental level, often with some accompanying inattentive features, across more than one setting and with functional impairment. In adults it often appears less as overt running or climbing and more as inner restlessness, constant activity, interrupting, blurting, and difficulty remaining seated. It is distinguished from episodic mood disorders, anxiety-driven agitation, or situational stress reactions by its chronic, trait-like course and consistent pattern of impairment.

patient.stressor: Isabella's presentation came into focus during a prolonged period of in-law troubles, when disagreements about family obligations and finances began intruding on evenings she had previously protected for yoga, painting, and careful procurement planning. Over 2 years and 2 months, the added strain made longstanding tendencies harder to compensate for: she missed details in vendor spreadsheets, appeared not to absorb direct questions in sourcing meetings, fidgeted through calls, and blurted responses during negotiations before others finished speaking. The impairment remained mild but real, showing up as corrected purchase-order errors, strained family dinners, and feedback that she was interrupting junior colleagues she meant to mentor. She raised the issue herself during a primary-care wellness visit after noticing the same pattern at work, home, and her STEM mentoring sessions, and was referred for psychiatric assessment.

S001.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors
S001.description: Often fails to give close attention to details or makes careless mistakes.
S001.manifestation: Over the past couple of years, I’ll think I’ve checked a vendor spreadsheet carefully, and then our planning coordinator catches that I transposed a SKU, missed a freight surcharge, or carried the wrong quantity into the purchase order.

S003.name: Listening_Difficulty
S003.description: Often does not seem to listen when spoken to directly.
S003.manifestation: In sourcing meetings or even at the dinner table, I can be looking right at someone while they ask me something, and a few seconds later I realize I only caught the last part and have to ask them to repeat it.

S010.name: Fidgeting
S010.description: Often fidgets with or taps hands or feet or squirms in seat.
S010.manifestation: On calls with suppliers, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk and I’m clicking a pen or twisting my ring so much that I have to mute myself or move my hands out of view.

S011.name: Leaving_Seat
S011.description: Often leaves seat in situations when remaining seated is expected.
S011.manifestation: If a meeting runs long or we’re having one of those tense family dinners with my in-laws, I keep finding reasons to get up for water, check the oven, or look at samples instead of just staying in my chair.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: What brings me in is this constant restless feeling, like I’m wound too tight and can’t fully settle, even when I’m supposed to be calmly sitting through a planning meeting, painting, or doing yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: Even on weekends, I tend to finish one thing and immediately start another—laundry, emails, reorganizing product samples, touching up a painting—while my husband says I never really power down.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: During vendor negotiations or STEM mentoring sessions, I sometimes jump in with an answer before the other person has finished the question, and then I realize I missed an important qualifier.

S018.name: Interrupting_Intruding
S018.description: Often interrupts or intrudes on others (e.g., butts into conversations, games, or activities).
S018.manifestation: I catch myself cutting into junior buyers’ conversations to correct a detail or add my opinion before they’ve asked for it, even though I’m trying to support them rather than take over.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: I remember in elementary school getting notes sent home because I kept popping out of my seat, talking over classmates, and rushing to answer before the teacher finished the question.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: At work it has led to corrected purchase orders and extra review from my planning coordinator, and at home it has made family dinners more tense because people feel talked over.
add_requirements.duration: It has been noticeably harder to manage for about 2 years and 2 months, since the in-law conflicts started taking over more of our evenings.
